v.why: Larger batches average out gradient noise, which stabilizes Adam at aggressive learning rates where small-batch updates are noise-dominated or diverge.
Wider layers amplify the function change per Adam step, so already-aggressive learning rates become unstable.
When width limits capacity, extra layers add compositional capacity that wide networks already have.
The L2 term is scaled by 1/batch size, so small batches amplify the penalty and raising alpha pushes toward underfitting.
Small batches give noisy gradients, so a larger learning rate drives noise-dominated or divergent updates.
Updates compound across layers in deep ReLU stacks, shrinking the stable learning-rate range.
Narrow networks have small per-step function change and tolerate larger rates, so raising the rate speeds fitting.
Smaller batches scale up the per-step L2 term, so strong alpha combined with small batches over-regularizes.
Large batches give few updates in 243 epochs, so deep nets undertrain and removing a layer speeds convergence.
Single-hidden-layer nets are width-limited, so widening supplies the missing capacity.
